content:
maria gomez: opened a follow-up PR to consolidate Dedicated provisioning notes. This one's focused on three small things: clearer autoscale policy examples, an SLA blurb that distinguishes preemption vs. eviction, and a short terraform+SDK snippet for creating a reserved pool. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/601

samir patel: thank you. two quick asks: (1) make the autoscale example show both target-based and schedule-based scaling; (2) call out that burst capacity can exceed advertised max replicas for a short period if spare GPUs are available. that last bit is important for customer expectations.

jo parks: i can add a tiny schedule example. like: scale to 10 replicas M-F 9-5, otherwise back to 2. will put it in a yaml snippet. also added a sentence about burst behavior but kept it in the operational notes rather than SLA.

jo parks: schedule snippet:
```yaml
scale_policy:
  type: scheduled
  entries:
    - cron: "0 9 * * 1-5"
      replicas: 10
    - cron: "0 17 * * 1-5"
      replicas: 2
```

alex chen: FYI i found a wording mismatch: the migration guide said "dedicated pools do not preempt" which is inaccurate — infra-level preemption can still occur depending on cloud provider and instance type. suggest: "Dedicated pools reduce platform-initiated disruptions; provider preemption may still occur."

maria gomez: good catch. jo, can you fold alex's suggested phrasing into the SLA paragraph? keep it short.

jo parks: updated SLA paragraph to: "Dedicated pools minimize platform-initiated evictions. Provider-level preemption (e.g., spot reclaim) is possible depending on instance family and region; see the glossary for definitions." linked glossary anchor.

nate hall: added a quantization/perf callout under the Private deployment section: "Quantized models may change latency and throughput characteristics; benchmark at expected sequence lengths." also added a brief note that caching helps hide some variance.

samir patel: can we include a CLI+terraform combo snippet for creating a reserved pool that the infra team can copy? i'll paste one i use in staging (sanitized).

samir patel: terraform snippet:
```hcl
resource "redwood_reserved_pool" "acme_pool" {
  name = "acme-prod-pool"
  region = "us-west-2"
  instance_type = "g4dn.xlarge"
  min_size = 2
  max_size = 8
  burst_enabled = true
}
```

samir patel: CLI snippet (bash):
```bash
redwood pool create --name acme-prod-pool --region us-west-2 --instance-type g4dn.xlarge --min 2 --max 8 --burst
```

maria gomez: perfect. alex, can you check the infra compat table? we added GPU family rows but want a simple note about typical throughput delta ranges, not absolute numbers.

alex chen: reviewed. i added a short column that says "typical throughput factor vs baseline (ballpark)" with values like "~0.7-1.3" and a big caveat link to infra benchmarks. removed an internal-only GPU SKU.

docs-bot: ran link-check. 1 remaining broken link (old terragrunt reference) flagged in migration appendix.

bench-bot: scheduled perf run for g4dn.xlarge and p4d. results ETA: 2024-06-18. will post numbers as ranges only.

nate hall: noted. also added a short FAQ Q: "Will my reserved pool stop serving during a provider preemption?" Answer: "Occasionally; we recommend leak-tolerant clients and configuration of fallback routing to hosted API for critical paths."

jo parks: moved terraform into appendix and kept concise SDK snippet in main content. tightened language across the page to reduce duplication.

samir patel: +1 to merging after bench numbers are placeholders. small nit: env var name in SDK example should be REDWOOD_POOL_ID (not REDWOOD_POOL). fixed in a later commit.

maria gomez: OK let's get a final thumbs. i'm aiming to merge this afternoon after bench-bot posts placeholder ranges.

jo parks: +1

samir patel: +1

alex chen: +1

nate hall: +1 (will update perf ranges when bench results come in)

maria gomez: merging in 20m if no objections. thanks for quick reviews, everyone! :tada:
